title: Support for PMETs in their 40s and 50s facing structural unemployment risks
asked: Mr Christopher de Souza asked for an assessment of structural unemployment risks facing Singaporean PMETs in their 40s and 50s, and whether the Ministry will strengthen measures for their re-employment, mid-career transitions and wage sustainability, and if so what measures.
response: Dr Koh said the long-term unemployment rate for resident PMETs in their 40s and 50s remained within the range seen in non-recessionary periods, indicating structural unemployment risks remain low and stable. He listed existing support: WSG’s Mid-Career Pathways Programme, SSG’s SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme, WSG’s Career Conversion Programmes with salary support for employers, and the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, with over $10 billion invested over five years. In supplementary replies, he said the Tripartite Workgroup for Senior Employment is looking at going upstream to prevent displacement, building a better career and employment ecosystem, and that NTUC already helps workers move across adjacent union sectors; he said a tight labour market is not the most appropriate tool for facilitating lateral movement.

key_points.point: The long-term unemployment rate for resident PMETs in their 40s and 50s remained within the range observed during non-recessionary periods.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: remained within the range observed during non-recessionary periods

key_points.quote: support mid-career jobseekers to acquire industry relevant experience and skills to facilitate career transitions

key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: provide employers with more salary support to reskill mature workers into growth job roles with good longer-term prospects

key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: can tap on SSG’s SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme

key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon

key_points.quote: that is one of the streams of work that the Tripartite Workgroup for Senior Employment is looking at

key_points.point: NTUC has a practice of helping workers potentially displaced from one union sector reach across other unions in adjacent sectors.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon

key_points.point: The focus is on making workers more aware of opportunities in adjacent sectors and helping them gain skills to pivot across.

key_points.quote: make sure that there is more awareness amongst the workers themselves where opportunities may lie in adjacent sectors

left_open: Wage sustainability for PMETs in their 40s and 50s.
Specific further measures the Ministry will consider for re-employment and mid-career transitions, beyond existing programmes and the Tripartite Workgroup's study.
Mentorship programmes in the IT and engineering sectors.
supplementary: Going beyond SkillsFuture, mentorship and lateral movement across related sectors, including through union structures.
